status: Virtual provider model, scheduler registration, template capture/heal and stream failover state machine verified against upstream src/virtual.ts through the VirtualHost trait; host cross-provider delegation binding pending (H-DELEG)
compared: Each scenario's complete ordered op outputs, complete ordered trace and final injected clock; the Rust test compares whole JSON values, JavaScript numbers by value

createVirtualIntegrations: scheduler ids, labels, selectionBias none, enabled-backend accounts, weights, metadata, maxAccountAttempts recorded but not enforced, duplicate backend and duplicate model registration errors
Transport-failure classification: status-less network messages, the unavailable prefix, and non-transport negatives including a non-ASCII codepoint inside 'Connection error'
Backend selection and resolveTarget: lookups, unavailable provider or model failover, backing model identity, ambient auth merge over caller options, base URL override, placeholder auth
Same-account tolerance (errorsBeforeSwitch) with 250 ms pauses, cancellation during the pause, response receipt reset per physical stream and classification by response status
Failover across backends, maxAccountAttempts bounds, onFailover surface/void/throw, implicit affinity hand-off and explicit pin retention, terminal replay of the last buffered start and error

Event forwarding: buffered latest start, durationMs stamping on terminal messages, abort handling, streamSimple kind forwarding

createVirtualProvider: models templated from live or persisted backends, disabled backends ignored, metadata fallback defaults, auth resolution with configured checks, template capture and heal (fill missing, keep existing, null template blocks healing)
Scheduling delegated to services.rs: round-robin and weights through the verified Service, rate-limit cooldowns, pins and affinity read through Service
The eighteen upstream virtual.spec.ts case names are asserted in the reference script against the upstream behaviour before fixture generation
limits: The VirtualHost trait is host-independent: the physical backing stream is an opaque fixture stream, not a real provider SDK or pi-ai stream.
The cross-provider delegation binding to the host is not implemented; the start/resolve_ambient_auth/backing_models hooks are the boundary a later lane must bind (H-DELEG).
Upstream's SDK-level request conversion (headers, env, baseUrl applied by the real backing provider) is not reproduced; only the options handed to the backing provider are compared.
The lazy-stream wrapper is modelled by Pending::drive and durationMs stamping of terminal messages; pi-ai's real AssistantMessageEventStream internals are not exercised.
Persistence of healed configs and the editor/config-file round trip are not part of this lane.
